statement: A unique observation in the dyadic interval gives the three-level Lomax sample exactly two global maximizers above the exponential limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃! a, a ∈ Ioo ((2 : ℝ) ^ 512)⁻¹ ((2 : ℝ) ^ 32)⁻¹ ∧
      let x : Fin 21 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i.val = 0 then a else if i.val ≤ 10 then 1 else 100
      ∃ p ∈ Lomax.domain, ∃ q ∈ Lomax.domain,
        p.2 < 1024 ∧ 1024 < q.2 ∧
        IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain p ∧
        IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain q ∧
        (∀ b ∈ Lomax.domain,
          IsMaxOn (fun v : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Lomax.logLik x v.1 v.2) Lomax.domain b → b = p ∨ b = q) ∧
        bestExp x < Lomax.logLik x p.1 p.2
dossier_scope_note: The other observations are ten copies each of 1 and 100. The two rates straddle 1024.

statement: The reciprocal Lomax sample has exactly two inverse Pareto maximizers above the inverse-exponential limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃ x : Fin 21 → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < x i) ∧
      ∃ p q : ℝ × ℝ, p.2 < q.2 ∧
        {v ∈ Lomax.domain | IsMaxOn (fun b : ℝ × ℝ ↦
          Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x b.1 b.2) Lomax.domain v} = {p, q} ∧
        Transfer.InvPareto.bestInvExp x < Transfer.InvPareto.logLik x p.1 p.2
dossier_scope_note: The reciprocal data map preserves both maximizing parameter pairs in shape and scale.

statement: For every held threshold there is a Pareto II sample with exactly two global maximizers above the shifted exponential limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
(μ : ℝ) :
    ∃ x : Fin 21 → ℝ, (∀ i, μ < x i) ∧
      ∃ p q : ℝ × ℝ, p.2 < q.2 ∧
        {v ∈ Lomax.domain | IsMaxOn (fun b : ℝ × ℝ ↦
          Transfer.ParetoII.logLik x μ b.1 b.2) Lomax.domain v} = {p, q} ∧
        Transfer.ParetoII.bestShiftedExp x μ < Transfer.ParetoII.logLik x μ q.1 q.2
dossier_scope_note: This sample has strictly positive excesses. Its two scales are reciprocals of the two Lomax rates.

statement: Reciprocation is a bijection of the complete joint maximizing sets on all positive samples.
dossier_scope_note: The shape is preserved and scale is inverted. The theorem also applies when both maximizing sets are empty.

statement: Reciprocal data and reciprocal held scale preserve the complete maximizing set of shapes.
dossier_scope_note: The statement is for every positive held scale and positive sample.

statement: The held-scale two-observation construction has a unique crossing and two global maximizers in the specified shape bands.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃! r, r ∈ Ioo (3 / 1000 : ℝ) (5 / 1000) ∧
      ∃ a ∈ Icc (2 : ℝ) 4, ∃ b ∈ Icc (6500 : ℝ) 10000,
        {k ∈ Ioi 0 | IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ Paralogistic.logLik
          (fun i ↦ exp (tieLogs r i)) t 1) (Ioi 0) k} = {a, b}
dossier_scope_note: The held scale is one. The complement of the bands is excluded by exact rational inequalities.

statement: The reciprocal two-observation sample has the same unique crossing and the same two maximizing shapes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃! r, r ∈ Ioo (3 / 1000 : ℝ) (5 / 1000) ∧
      ∃ a ∈ Icc (2 : ℝ) 4, ∃ b ∈ Icc (6500 : ℝ) 10000,
        {k ∈ Ioi 0 | IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ InvParalogistic.logLik
          (fun i ↦ exp (-(tieLogs r i))) t 1) (Ioi 0) k} = {a, b}

statement: The source two-level all-free sample has a unique crossing with exactly two global maximizers.
dossier_scope_note: The complete maximizing set is a pair whose shapes straddle 1/10000.

statement: The reciprocal all-free sample has exactly two global maximizers at its unique crossing.
dossier_scope_note: The forward and inverse joint maximizing sets correspond under inversion of scale.

statement: Nine ones and one outlier yield a global tie between the exponential member and a separated positive-shape fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃ m ∈ Ioo (81 / 10 : ℝ) 128,
      let x : Fin 10 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i = 0 then m else 1
      let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik x p.1 p.2
      let p₀ := (exponentialRate x, 0)
      p₀ ∈ jointDomain ∧ IsMaxOn f jointDomain p₀ ∧
        ∃ b > (117 / 200 : ℝ), ∃ η > (0 : ℝ),
          (b, η) ∈ jointDomain ∧ IsMaxOn f jointDomain (b, η)
dossier_scope_note: The outlier is proved to exist in (8.1, 128). The number of positive-shape winners is open.

statement: There is a unique transition in the sample path with 99 repeated observations and one 1 where the half-normal ties a positive-location fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    ∃! e, e ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (1 / 5) ∧
      let x : Fin 100 → ℝ := fun i ↦ if i = 0 then 1 else e
      let S : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Ici 0 ×ˢ Ioi 0
      let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik x p.1 p.2
      (0, m₂ x) ∈ S ∧ IsMaxOn f S (0, m₂ x) ∧
        ∃ μ > (0 : ℝ), ∃ t > (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn f S (μ, t)
dossier_scope_note: Variance is the second coordinate. The theorem does not count the positive-location winners.

statement: At held alpha 2 the shapes (1, 100) beat every diagonal point on counts (0, 200).
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    let p (r b : ℝ) (k : ℕ) :=
      (Gamma (2 + r) * Gamma (2 + b) * Gamma (r + k) * Gamma (b + k)) /
        (Gamma (2 + r + b + k) * Gamma r * Gamma b * k.factorial)
    ∀ d > 0, p d d 0 * p d d 200 < p 1 100 0 * p 1 100 200
dossier_scope_note: Uses the explicit probability product on an alternative sample. Transport to the imported log likelihood and the golden-sample comparison remain open.

statement: The explicit likelihood of (0, 200) at alpha 2 has two distinct swapped global maximizers.
hypotheses_and_conclusion:
:
    let mass (r b : ℝ) (k : ℕ) :=
      (Gamma (2 + r) * Gamma (2 + b) * Gamma (r + k) * Gamma (b + k)) /
        (Gamma (2 + r + b + k) * Gamma r * Gamma b * k.factorial)
    let S : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioi 0
    let f := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ mass p.1 p.2 0 * mass p.1 p.2 200
    ∃ p ∈ S, p.1 ≠ p.2 ∧ IsMaxOn f S p ∧ p.swap ∈ S ∧ IsMaxOn f S p.swap
dossier_scope_note: Uses the explicit probability product. It proves at least two labeled fits to the same distribution.
